16: On the sixth day, soft music came from behind the star door.
Four points were shining, and one was still dark.
Kori pressed her ear to the door and listened.
Kiri closed her eyes and began to hum the tune.
The little island kitten hummed along, very quietly.
Pip the robot blinked his lights in time with the song.
The last point flickered, like a tiny firefly.
But when the song stopped, the light went out again.
Kori sang louder, but the point stayed dark.
Kiri noticed five small paw marks around the door.
Abram counted them from the bridge: five marks for five friends.
That day, the kittens learned that some songs need every voice.
17: On the seventh day, the kittens counted their friends.
Kiri, Kori, the island kitten and Pip made four.
The fifth friend was their old white teacher.
But the teacher had never crossed the bridge of light.
Kori ran back to the school to bring him.
The teacher looked at the glowing bridge and trembled.
Kiri walked beside him, one slow step at a time.
Pip floated ahead and lit the way like a small moon.
In the middle, the teacher stopped and looked down at the clouds.
The little island kitten ran out and touched his nose.
Together they reached the island, and the teacher smiled.
That day, the kittens learned that even teachers need a brave friend.
18: On the eighth day, five friends stood before the star door.
Each one sat down on a small paw mark.
Kiri began the song, soft and low.
Kori joined in, bright and happy.
The little island kitten sang in a tiny voice.
The old teacher purred deep, like a warm drum.
Pip added a sparkle of light to every note.
The fifth point of the star door began to shine.
All five points glowed together like a small sun.
Slowly, without a sound, the star door opened.
Behind it, a path of silver light led up into the sky.
That day, the kittens learned that together they can open any door.
19: On the ninth day, the friends climbed the path of light.
At the top was a quiet garden above the clouds.
Hundreds of tiny stars were sleeping in the silver grass.
They were baby stars, too small to shine in the sky.
One little star rolled to Kori and tickled her paw.
Kiri picked one up gently, and it began to glow.
The old teacher knew why: stars wake up when someone holds them kindly.
So each friend held a star close and purred.
One by one, the baby stars grew warm and bright.
Pip lifted them softly up into the evening sky.
Abram watched the first new stars appear above the school.
That day, the kittens learned that gentle paws can light the sky.
20: On the tenth day, the sky above the school was full of new stars.
The kittens walked back across the bridge of light.
The little island kitten stopped at the edge of the island.
It had no school, and no family of its own.
Kori turned around and held out her paw.
Kiri made room beside her on the bridge.
The old teacher had one more cushion waiting in the classroom.
The little kitten took one small step, and then another.
Abram welcomed it with a soft lick on the head.
That night, three kittens fell asleep under the glass dome.
Above them, the baby stars twinkled like friends saying good night.
That day, the kittens learned that home is where your friends are.
